messages:
nora: FYI we've got a bunch of mypy/pyright failures when using the new python-sdk generated clients in the payments service. Seems related to the response typing shape.

akash: can you paste one of the concrete errors?

nora: heres one from CI: 

```
payments/services/redwood_client.py:88: error: Expression of type "str" cannot be assigned to declared type "Optional[str]"  [assignment]
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 42 source files)
```

nora: root cause appears to be generator emitting Pydantic models for domain objects but response parsing in clients still typed as Mapping[str, Any] -> runtime ends up with plain str, mypy flags assignment to Optional[str].

sergio: interesting. Our old generator produced TypedDicts for responses which played nicely with static checkers. When we moved to Pydantic models we forgot to also generate typed response stubs.

akash: options: a) regenerate responses as TypedDicts, b) make model attributes Any, c) add `# type: ignore` at assignment sites, d) add an opt-in flag for clients to emit stricter types.

nora: (c) and (b) feel like bandaids. For teams that enable strict typing we should offer (a) or (d). Prefer (d) so we can ship without breaking for everyone.

sergio: agreed. I'll prototype a `--typed-responses` CLI option for the openapi generator. If passed, we emit a TypedDict for each operation response and update the client stubs to use those.

nora: will that help pyright too? Some of our infra uses pyright in VSCode and errors are similar.

sergio: yes TypedDicts are understood by pyright and mypy. Also planning to add `from __future__ import annotations` at top of generated modules to reduce forward-reference quirkiness.

devx-bot: Branch push detected: feature/typed-resp-gen (repo: python-sdk)

akash: also noticed embedding arrays are typed as List[Any] in several models. That trips developers expecting List[float]. Is there a schema hint we can use?

sergio: we'll add heuristic: if json schema type is array with items type=number -> use List[float]. If items are ambiguous -> List[Any]. We'll include a note in the changelog.

nora: one more ask: can we include an async sample app that demonstrates consuming typed responses with the AsyncClient? Current examples are all sync and minimal. It would really lower onboarding friction.

sergio: yes, adding an async sample that imports generated TypedDicts and shows `async with RedwoodAsyncClient() as c:` + mypy config. Will also include a pyrightconfig.json sample.

akash: good call to add migration docs. I can help draft a short guide: "Upgrading to 0.9.x: enabling typed responses" with code snippets and a small replace script to add casts temporarily.

qa-bot: nightly typecheck: job scheduled for branch feature/typed-resp-gen (mypy+pyright)

nora: for short-term unblockers we've patched callers with `from typing import cast, Optional` and `model.name = cast(Optional[str], resp.get("name"))` but this is noisy. Would like SDK fix asap.

sergio: ETA: WIP PR by EOD with the flag and tests. If the team likes it we'll flip default in 1.0.0. I'll also add unit tests that run mypy over a small sample package.

akash: awesome. @sergio please ping when PR is up — I'll add CI job that runs pyright as well. :thumbsup:

nora: thanks — this will make life much easier for teams that enforce types strictly.

sergio: thanks folks. PR will include async sample, changelog entry, and a note about embedding types. Will post link here once open.

devx-bot: CI pipeline started for feature/typed-resp-gen (mypy stage)
